title: Rotation-aware Reminder Orchestrator and Noise Attenuation Hub
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Pager/notification fatigue during noisy rotations remains a major contributor to oncall burnout and missed actions. This PR introduces a lightweight orchestration layer for scheduled reminders that is rotation-aware and adaptive to recent alert noise. The feature provides per-rotation attenuation, smart backoff, and a simple opt-out path for individuals. Design summary: 1) A RemindOrchestrator service that consumes schedule snapshots and recent-alert-rate signals to compute a reminder cadence per oncall rotation slot. 2) A NoiseAttenuation policy module that applies exponential backoff, minimum/maximum cadence bounds, and a sliding-window noise score (persisted to Redis with TTL) so attenuation survives restarts but decays over time. 3) Slack + Email adapters that respect user-level opt-outs and per-rotation override flags. 4) Observability: new metrics (slo.reminders.sent, slo.reminders.attenuation_ratio, slo.reminders.opt_out_count) and traces for reminder decision paths. 5) Safety and rollout: default to conservative behavior (no reminders for rotations with >30 alerts/hour until attenuation decays), feature flag gating, and a canary rollout to 10% of rotations. This PR includes unit and integration tests, documentation updates, and a short runbook for oncall responders (see docs/runbooks/reminder-orchestrator.md). Backwards compatibility: existing reminder endpoints remain available; orchestrator runs as an opt-in feature. Rollback plan: flip feature flag off; orchestrator is stateless aside from Redis TTLs and can be disabled without disruption. Related: ENG-2314 (oncall fatigue reduction), ENG-2317 (reminder metrics), SUP-987 (support request about missed escalations).
